Let
\[
p(\lambda)=1+c_1\lambda+c_2\lambda^2+c_3\lambda^3.
\]
The admissible Richardson cubics are exactly the relevant minimax cubics with \(p(0)=1\) and three positive zeros; positivity follows in each case from the alternating signs below.

For four ordered active points \(a<b<c<d\), the cubic with values
\[
p(a)=C,\quad p(b)=-C,\quad p(c)=C,\quad p(d)=-C
\]
is optimal whenever its absolute value stays below \(C\) on \(E_\gamma\). Indeed, any better cubic would differ from it by a cubic vanishing at \(0\) and changing sign in each of the three gaps between active points, hence would have at least four zeros.

Now consider the endpoint-alternating cubic \(h_\gamma\), normalized by
\[
h_\gamma(1)=1,\quad h_\gamma(2)=-1,\quad h_\gamma(\gamma)=1,\quad h_\gamma(6)=-1.
\]
The actual minimizer is \(p_\gamma^*=h_\gamma/h_\gamma(0)\) exactly while no interior extremum enters either interval.

Using the Lagrange formula for \(h_\gamma'\), the two endpoint tangency tests are
\[
h_\gamma'(\gamma)=0
\iff
(\gamma-1)^2(\gamma^2-14\gamma+44)=0,
\]
and
\[
h_\gamma'(2)=0
\iff
(\gamma-1)(\gamma^2-9\gamma+19)=0.
\]
In the given range, these give
\[
\gamma_1=7-\sqrt5,
\qquad
\gamma_2=\frac{9+\sqrt5}{2}.
\]

The active sets are therefore:

\[
\frac92<\gamma<7-\sqrt5:
\qquad
\mathcal A_\gamma=\{1,2,7-\sqrt5,6\}.
\]
Here the right-interval interior maximum \(7-\sqrt5\) is active, while the endpoint \(\gamma\) is inactive.

\[
7-\sqrt5<\gamma<\frac{9+\sqrt5}{2}:
\qquad
\mathcal A_\gamma=\{1,2,\gamma,6\}.
\]

\[
\frac{9+\sqrt5}{2}<\gamma<\frac{17}{3}:
\qquad
\mathcal A_\gamma=\{1,\tau_\gamma,\gamma,6\},
\]
where \(\tau_\gamma\in(1,2)\) is the unique interior critical point with \(p_\gamma^*(\tau_\gamma)=-\mathcal C_\gamma^*\).

At \(\gamma=\gamma_1\), the active point \(7-\sqrt5\) coincides with the left endpoint of the right interval and is tangent:
\[
\mathcal A_{\gamma_1}=\{1,2,\gamma_1,6\},\qquad (p_{\gamma_1}^*)'(\gamma_1)=0.
\]
At \(\gamma=\gamma_2\), the point \(2\) is tangent:
\[
\mathcal A_{\gamma_2}=\{1,2,\gamma_2,6\},\qquad (p_{\gamma_2}^*)'(2)=0.
\]

Thus the requested pair is
\[
\boxed{\left(7-\sqrt5,\frac{9+\sqrt5}{2}\right)}.
\]
